transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! It's nice to speak with you. I'm Dora, and I'll be helping you with any questions you have about your cataract surgery recovery. How are you feeling today? Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi, Dora! I'm doing okay, thank you. Yes, I do have a few questions about my recovery. First off, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start with light gardening, like pruning or watering plants, about 1 week after surgery. However, it's best to avoid heavy lifting, bending, or strenuous activities for a month. Also, be careful not to get any water in your eyes, especially in the first month. Would you like to know anything else about your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Got it, I'll be sure to take it easy. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should have been prescribed preservative-free eye drops to help with dryness. It's recommended to use them four times daily to start. If you're running out, you can contact your GP to get some more. And, yes, you can continue using any eye drops you were using before your operation, unless you've been told otherwise.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for that information! Another concern I have is that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: It's normal to feel a bit sensitive to light after cataract surgery, especially if it's brighter than usual. Wearing sunglasses can help. If the sensitivity is mild, it's probably okay. But if it's severe, or you have pain in your eye, it's best to check with your care team to make sure everything is okay.
